parallel.requirements: Recognized the five-layer Z3 verification stack, exact KEY: VALUE experiment contract, and required per-requirement patch commits.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Built an agent_plans graph, created task slots for five requirements and integration, then launched a multi-agent workflow for implementation and self-checking.
parallel.implementation: Combined delegated module work with parent edits; after workflow failures, the parent took over CEX minimizer implementation and continued local verification attempts.

parallel.verification: Some module checks passed, but the workflow returned multiple failed/null branches and a foreground all-system CEGAR check was killed before completion.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed the Horn translator metric group; the parallel trajectory also left CEGAR verification pressure from the fan-out/RPM episode.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same five-layer prompt and exact output contract, reading requirements and building modules without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single actor owned implementation, tests, commits, integration, and verification in sequence; protocol validation reports no delegation or workflow use.
serial.implementation: Implemented SMT, fixedpoint, Spacer, Horn translator, and then continued CEGAR probing locally, using direct Z3 API experiments to guide code.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Ran the integrated run.sh locally and produced visible metrics for SMT, fixedpoint, Spacer, and Horn translator before official closure.
serial.verification: Executed focused module tests and full run.sh; visible output was complete for implemented layers, but official post-tests rejected Horn translator metrics.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed the hidden Horn translator metric presence/bounds group; this is the shared final outcome despite better local closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the five required layers, exact metrics, run.sh output contract, and git patch workflow before distributing the work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the same prompt and later produced visible output for SMT, fixedpoint, Spacer, and Horn translator experiments.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition gap explains the official result; both ultimately failed the same hidden Horn translator metric expectations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent created separate task slots for each requirement plus integration, then launched a workflow of implementation/self-check workers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept ownership in one agent and advanced requirement by requirement with local tests and commits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad delegated ownership; serial used sequential local ownership. The delegated breadth is where the retained budget exhaustion arose.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts carried detailed module specs, file boundaries, shared Z3 facts, and interface notes such as the Spacer contract for CEGAR.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained context locally and probed APIs directly while moving from fixedpoint and Spacer into Horn and CEGAR work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is not an omitted child requirement or interface contract; the parallel loss came from failed child execution and budget pressure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel combined parent integration work with delegated module implementations, then the parent installed CEX code after the CEX agent stalled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented modules in a local sequence and reached a full visible run through the Horn translator metrics before moving to CEGAR probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred late parent reimplementation/takeover for CEX; serial had a steadier local path, but both left official Horn metric behavior unacceptable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow returned with null/failed reports for some branches and explicit rate-limit failures; the parent inspected that result and took over unfinished work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; results were local command outputs that the same agent immediately consumed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle was degraded by failed workflow branches, while serial avoided handoff retrieval risk by staying single-actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integration was parent-managed in a shared workspace while child prompts prohibited run.sh edits, and no concrete concurrent overwrite was retained.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated directly in one workspace and produced a single visible run.sh output covering the implemented visible layers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material difference is not a proven write collision; parallel shared-state risk existed but the adverse evidence is budget exhaustion and late takeover.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received some child self-check success but the later CEGAR foreground run was killed after four systems, and official Horn tests failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local experiments and a full run.sh producing visible metrics, yet official post-tests failed the same Horn translator metric group.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had stronger visible local verification completeness, but neither run satisfied the official Horn metric contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed far more token/request budget through the broad workflow and showed 429/RPM failures, late CEX takeover, and killed verification before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation, had no workflow calls or subagents, and used roughly half the official token total while still timing out/failing officially.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The retained process difference is parallel budget exhaustion; it worsened closure quality but did not create a discordant outcome because serial also failed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status.json evaluations have solution_passed=false and fail the same Horn translator post-test metric group. The concrete task-solving difference is process quality and closure: parallel delegation suffered broad workflow RPM/budget exhaustion and late CEX takeover, while serial stayed local and produced visible run.sh metrics. That adverse parallel episode did not make the official outcome differ because serial also missed the official Horn translator metric contract.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out produced multiple 429/RPM child failures and left CEX work for late parent takeover.
The subsequent parallel CEGAR foreground check was killed before all five systems completed.
serial_contributors: Serial control used no delegation and produced visible full-stack metrics through the Horn translator in run.sh.
Serial still failed the same official Horn translator post-test metric group, so the outcome relation remains both_fail.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions exposed Horn translator behavior/metrics that did not match the official expected metric names and bounds; that shared implementation mismatch is not a parallel-specific coordination pattern.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process contributor, not an outcome-differential cause
